name: Shanghai International Marathon
summary: The Shanghai International Marathon runs point to point from the Bund to Xujiahui Sports Park. It passes Nanjing Road, Jing'an Temple, Huaihai Road and Xintiandi. A race listing describes the profile as flat. It has been held from late November to early December in recent years.
courseHighlights: Start at the Bund Bull Plaza on the Huangpu River
West Bund riverfront on Longteng Avenue

paceStrategy.summary: Sources describe a flat course, so even pacing works. Cool weather helps. Keep your effort steady through the city streets and save energy for the last stretch on Longhua Road.

segments.advice: Start at goal pace or a touch slower; the opening streets are crowded.

segments.terrain: City streets: Jing'an Temple, Huaihai Road, Xintiandi
segments.advice: Hold goal pace through the city centre.

segments.terrain: Later stretch along the West Bund riverfront (Longteng Avenue)
segments.advice: Stay steady on the open riverside road, where wind can matter.

segments.terrain: Inland on Longhua Road to the finish
segments.advice: Keep your form and push to the line.

fuelingNotes: The sources I used do not list aid-station positions, so check the official runner guide. In cool weather, take gels about every 40 minutes and sip fluids at each station.
tips: The route can change before race day, so check the official final course
Dress warmly for the early start, as race-morning temperatures are low
Plan transport to the Bund start, as roads close early

faq.question: Is the Shanghai Marathon flat?
faq.answer: A race listing describes the profile as flat. A guide gives about 25–30 m of total climbing.

faq.question: Where does the Shanghai Marathon start and finish?
faq.answer: It starts at Bund Bull Plaza and finishes at Xujiahui Sports Park, according to recent listings. Earlier years finished at Shanghai Stadium and the West Bund Art Center.

faq.question: When is the Shanghai Marathon held?
faq.answer: Recent editions were held in late November or early December.
